quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake suddenly to stop your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Press the brakes gently and increase pressure slowly so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: You see a green light ahead, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Don't enter until you can drive completely across.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter until you can drive completely across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, don't enter if you can't get all the way across before it turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: The right way to make a right turn is to:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane nearest the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane nearest the right curb before turning.
Stay near the right curb as you approach, then move toward the middle before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane nearest the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal before turning to warn other drivers. Slow down and approach from the right lane, staying close to the right curb or edge.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity relate to speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speed causes longer stopping distances and more severe crashes. Increase your following distance at higher speeds to stop safely if needed.

questions.question: Hydroplaning can happen when water is on the road. At what speed might your car start to hydroplane?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: At speeds up to 35 mph, tires push water away. Above 35 mph, tires can't move water fast enough, and your tires may lift off the road like water skis.

questions.question: You have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Let pedestrians cross first.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in the intersection, even with a green light. Drivers must always yield to pedestrians when turning on a green light.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice:

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change speed and direction slowly and gradually.
Drive the same as normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change speed and direction slowly and gradually.
questions.explanation: Make gradual speed and direction changes on snow or ice. Don't use cruise control because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing a vehicle?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to move over.
After you signal for three seconds.
When you see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you have enough space before returning to your lane. Check your rearview mirror. When you see both headlights of the passed vehicle, you have enough room to move back.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are near.
Yield to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that bicycles may be crossing the road.

questions.question: If you are arrested for DUI and refuse a breath test, your license will be suspended for at least:

options.text: 14 days.
45 days.
21 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: 45 days.
questions.explanation: If you refuse a breath test, your license will be suspended for at least 45 days. You may also be required to install an ignition interlock device to get your license back.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: You see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction zone signs warn you of workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: You are entering an interstate highway. What should you do?

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough to safely enter the flow of traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps to merge into.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood may affect your:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment and coordination, even below the legal limit. Even small amounts can impair safe driving and lead to criminal charges.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Improves your ability to react to hazards.
Often leads to risky decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to risky decisions.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a common cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to risky decisions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: No passing zone signs and markings tell you that:

options.text: Oncoming cars are passing in your direction.
You can only pass during daylight.
You cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely.
questions.explanation: No passing zones are dangerous because you cannot see far enough ahead. These include intersections, railroad crossings, and shopping center entrances.

questions.question: Backing up your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Only dangerous in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road widens.
Right lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers that the right lane is ending. Prepare for traffic merging from the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge right.
Divided highway begins.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane ends ahead. Drivers in that lane will need to merge.

questions.question: You should check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. Do not stare at one spot. This helps you know where other vehicles are near you.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you:

options.text: Must give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to be a problem.
Must yield only to vehicles on your right.
Should slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must give the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to be a problem.
questions.explanation: When you see a yield sign, let other traffic go first if they are in your path. Be ready to stop. You can keep going if no other cars are coming.

questions.question: In rain or fog, you should use your:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help others see your car, even if they do not help you see much better.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drinking alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are under the legal blood alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts your judgment. You need good judgment to react to things on the road. Any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a downhill ramp that curves. You should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Wait until you enter the curve to start braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before you enter a curve. You may not be able to see what is ahead. Braking in a curve may cause your car to skid.
